text:
Maya: Quick weekly pulse — attaching p95/p99 tail numbers we pulled for NeoEdge this week by route + model, streaming vs non-streaming. Noting some spikes on a few routes. Can folks scan and call out anything suspicious?

Jonah: saw the dump — /generate on model Llama-13b-q shows streaming p99 ~1.9s up from 0.9s last week. p95 mostly stable.

Priya: that one jumped after last Friday's quantization rollout? Might be KV-cache priming + small batch sizes on streaming.

Maya: yes rollout on 13b-quant landed 2026-03-18. Numbers (minute summary) below:
```
route           | model            | mode       | p95   | p99
/generate       | Llama-13b-q      | streaming  | 420ms | 1900ms
/generate       | Llama-13b-q      | sync       | 360ms | 1150ms
/summary        | Llama-13b-q      | streaming  | 180ms | 260ms
/summary        | Llama-13b-q      | sync       | 170ms | 250ms
/rewrite        | Redw-7b-v2       | streaming  | 95ms  | 210ms
/rewrite        | Redw-7b-v2       | sync       | 88ms  | 190ms
```

EngBot: alert created: tail-latency-anomaly/neoedge/2061122329 — affected 0.7% of requests on /generate (streaming) during 03:15-03:20 UTC; higher KV miss ratio reported.

Jonah: KV miss fits. Streaming streams new requests and misses early prefixes — p99 blows up when a few long responses hit. Do we have batching config for NeoEdge on streaming?

Maya: NeoEdge streaming uses continuous-batch-size = 4, max-latency-ms = 30. They also have prefix-caching enabled but with TTL 1m.

Priya: proposed mitigations: increase continuous-batch-size to 8 (improves throughput), extend prefix TTL to 5m for stable patterns, and enable aggressive KV sticky routing for this customer for 24h to warm caches. Also recommend fallback to sync for very-long output routes during peak if p99 > 1s.

Ava (NeoEdge): thanks — curious about cost impact if we bump batch size / TTL? We need a sense for spend delta before approving.

Maya: rough estimate: batching to 8 reduces per-token compute by ~6% at our observed concurrency; TTL increase negligible cost but helps hit-rate. Fallback to sync will increase latency for some flows but reduce streaming p99 and lowers token overhead in retries. I'll get an exact delta and follow up in tomorrow's email.

Jonah: I'll queue a canary change on staging with batch-size=8 and TTL=5m, run 1 hour ramp at 10% of traffic. EngBot will post results.

EngBot: will do — scheduled canary at 03:40 UTC, rollback at 04:40 unless opt-in.

Maya: action items: 1) Jonah -> run canary (in progress). 2) Priya -> draft note for NeoEdge about temporary sticky routing and expected behavior. 3) Maya -> cost delta estimate + follow-up. 4) Ava -> confirm if sync-fallback acceptable for a short maintenance window.

Ava (NeoEdge): ok, sync-fallback is fine for a 30-60m window if it stabilizes user-facing timeouts. Please ping once canary completes. :thumbsup:

Maya: thanks team — I'll post canary results and cost numbers in this thread.
